summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was readmitted three days after discharge due to generalized weakness and hyperkalemia with a potassium level of 6.1. She was treated with intravenous calcium, insulin, and glucose, followed by urgent hemodialysis, which normalized her potassium. Her left upper extremity deep vein thrombosis was stable on warfarin with a therapeutic INR, and she remained on anticoagulation. Mild pulmonary edema was noted on chest imaging, attributed to fluid overload. Elevated aldolase and LDH levels raised concern for possible myopathy, prompting rheumatology follow-up. The patient improved clinically, was discharged home in stable condition, and instructed to continue warfarin with INR monitoring during dialysis and to follow up on pending lab results.
